{{Quote|Welcome to Sunspot Prison. The biggest, baddest penitentiary the Alliance has to offer. May your stay here be a short one.|Sunspot Prison's warden|<ref name="Star Wars 16" />}}
'''Sunspot Prison''', also known as '''Sunspot''', was a [[Space station|space-bound]] [[Prison|penitentiary]] maintained by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Reflecting its name, the prison orbited a [[star]] and was used to house the worst [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] prisoners that the Alliance captured. In [[0 ABY]], Sunspot Prison was [[Prison siege at Sunspot|raided]] by the rogue rebel agent [[Eneb Ray]] in an attempt to convince [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] to become a more ruthless leader. Ray's attack killed many prisoners and forced the closure of the prison. Sunspot Prison was later in use by the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]].

==Description==
Based in [[Standard Galactic Grid]] square I-18 in the [[Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="SWGalaxyMap" /> Sunspot [[Prison]] owed its name to a nearby [[Star|sun]] that bathed the [[orbit]]al [[space station]] in constant warmth and bright light. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the penitentiary hosted many [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[prisoner]]s including [[Spy|spies]], [[Mercenary|mercenaries]], war criminals, and even Imperial [[Moff|Moffs]]. Its existence was a well-guarded secret and most members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Alliance]] knew nothing about it. The prison was protected by a sea of [[ion cannon]]s at its front and had the sun at its back.<ref name="Star Wars 16" />

Sunspot Prison had numerous cells with metal grills that were guarded by [[armor]]ed [[rebel trooper]]s.<ref name="Star Wars 16" /> The prison also had a control center that could control the prison's sun shields.<ref name="Star Wars 17" /> Sunspot Prison also had a large [[hangar]] bay that was big enough to host the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''.<ref name="Star Wars 18" /> The command center also had an ion pulse that was capable of disrupting the station's power and [[gravity]].<ref name="Star Wars 19">[[Star Wars (2015) 19|''Star Wars'' (2015) 19]]</ref>

==History==
===Establishment===
{{Quote|Welcome to a place that doesn't officially exist.|Sunspot Prison's warden|<ref name="Star Wars 16" />}}
Sunspot Prison was established by the Rebel Alliance to house Imperial prisoners during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. By [[0 ABY]], its inmates included several Imperial [[soldier]]s including [[Kolar Ludd]], spies, mercenaries, war criminals, and at least two [[Moff]]s.<ref name="Star Wars 16" />

===Eneb Ray's assault===
{{Quote|Dr. Chelli Lona Aphra remanded to our max security penitentiary at Sunspot.|[[Arhul Narra|Commander Narra (Red Leader)]]|<ref name="TRF">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>}}
After being captured by [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and [[Sana Starros]] during the [[battle of Vrogas Vas]], the rogue [[archaeologist]] [[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra]], who had been a servant of [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], was questioned by [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service]] for [[Standard week|weeks]] but gave up no information. Sometime later, she was transported to Sunspot Prison. Shortly after Organa, Starros, and Aphra arrived at the prison, it was was [[Prison siege at Sunspot|raided]]<ref name="Star Wars 16" /> by the rogue rebel [[agent]] [[Eneb Ray]].<ref name="Star Wars 19" /> Following the failed [[Arrth-Eno Mission]],<ref name="Annual 1">[[Star Wars Annual (2015) 1|''Star Wars Annual'' (2015) 1]]</ref> Ray had embarked on a campaign to kill Imperial prisoners and to convince Organa to become a more ruthless leader.<ref name="Star Wars 19" />

After taking over the command center, Ray and his [[IG-RM bodyguard and enforcer droid]]s slaughtered numerous Imperial prisoners, by gunning them down in their cells and exposing the prisoners to the sun by lifting the sun shields<ref name="Star Wars 17" /> or throwing them out the [[airlock]]. Ray's rampage forced Organa, Starros, and Aphra to join forces to stop him.<ref name="Star Wars 18" />

Starros managed to send a [[distress signal]] to the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]].<ref name="Star Wars 18" /> Despite Ray taking [[Han Solo]] and [[Luke Skywalker]] hostage and playing mind games, Organa, Starros, and Aphra were able to subdue him with the help of [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]], who ignited an ion pulse that disrupted the station's gravity. Though Ray's rampage killed numerous Imperial prisoners, Organa's actions managed to save a few who were subsequently evacuated. Aphra escaped with the connivance of Organa and Starros. Despite being captured, Ray managed to escape and swore vengeance against Organa for spurning him.<ref name="Star Wars 19" />

After the Alliance closed the facility, members of the Imperial [[Task Force 99]] visited the prison searching for [[Kolar Ludd]]. They then departed on a mission to hunt down rebels.<ref name="Star Wars 19" /> Due to the assault, the Alliance was forced to temporarily close the facility, establishing a temporary [[Rebel Alliance holding facility|holding spot]] on [[Akiva]].<ref name="Star Wars 35">[[Star Wars (2015) 35|''Star Wars'' (2015) 35]]</ref>

===Back up and running===
The prison was still operating after the [[Battle of Endor]]. Following their disillusionment with the Empire, [[Inferno Squad]] feared surrendering to the Alliance, believing they might be imprisoned there.<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>

After the end of the [[Galactic Civil War]], the prison continued to operate under the [[New Republic]].<ref name="Chapter 14" /> In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|14}}</ref> the [[Tusken Raider]] [[Torbill Danzin (Tusken Raider)|Torbill Danzin]] was being held in Sunspot Prison for the attempted kidnapping of a New Republic [[senator]], serving a 25-[[Standard year|year]] sentence. [[Nilox Cabin-Roves]] was being held in Sunspot Prison for forgery of [[New Republic]] [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], serving a 20-[[Standard year|year]] sentence. [[Mon Calamari]] criminal [[Ghosla Fular]] was being held in Sunspot Prison for forgery of local [[currency]], serving a 30-[[Standard year|year]] sentence.<ref name="Chapter 14">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Sunspot Prison first appeared in the [[2016]] [[Marvel Comics|comic]] [[Star Wars (2015) 16|''Star Wars'' (2015) 16]], written by [[Jason Aaron]] and drawn by [[Leinil Francis Yu]].<ref name="Star Wars 16" />
